abstract: OBJECTIVES: Elevated tumor markers after primary chemotherapy for metastatic testis cancer are usually an indication of persistent cancer. Subsequent treatment has usually been salvage chemotherapy. This article examines the possibility that selected patients can achieve long-term disease-free survival with surgery alone. METHODS: Using a computerized data base of 627 postinduction chemotherapy retroperitoneal lymph node dissections (PC-RPLND), 23 patients with elevated tumor markers who have undergone PC-RPLND after induction chemotherapy alone were identified. Of the 23 patients, 15 were considered candidates for salvage chemotherapy, but instead underwent salvage surgery. Case histories were reviewed to establish selection criteria for PC-RPLND. RESULTS: Eight patients originally presented as clinical Stage C, 6 as clinical Stage B-3, and 1 as clinical Stage B-2. All patients initially received cisplatin combination chemotherapy. Twelve patients had an elevated alpha-fetoprotein level and 3 patients had an elevated beta human chorionic gonadotropin level prior to PC-RPLND. Seven patients had rising markers at the time of PC-RPLND. Seven patients had teratoma only in their resected specimen and all have no evidence of disease (NED) at a median of 35 months. Two patients had necrosis only in their RPLND specimen and both are NED at 10 and 42 months. Six patients had cancer in their resected specimen and 2 are NED, 1 is alive with disease, and 3 are dead of disease. Five of the 6 patients with cancer in their resected specimen were the only patients who received postoperative chemotherapy. CONCLUSIONS: Some patients with modest elevations of tumor markers after induction chemotherapy may only have teratoma or necrosis in the postchemotherapy resected specimen. These patients (n = 9) remain continuously NED. Patients who undergo salvage surgery and have cancer in the resected specimen do less well, but selected patients can be cured with this modality and thus avoid the morbidity of salvage chemotherapy.
abstract_ja: 目的：転移性精巣がんに対する初回化学療法後に腫瘍マーカーが上昇している場合、通常は残存がんを示すことが多く、その後の治療は救援化学療法が一般的であった。本研究では、手術のみで長期無病生存を得られる患者がいるかを検討した。方法：化学療法後後腹膜リンパ節郭清(PC-RPLND)を施行された627例のコンピュータデータベースから、初回導入化学療法のみを受け、腫瘍マーカーの上昇を伴ってPC-RPLNDを受けた23例を抽出した。このうち15例は救援化学療法の適応と考えられたが、代わりに救援手術を受けた。症例歴を見直し、PC-RPLNDの適応基準を検討した。結果：8例は臨床病期C、6例は臨床病期B-3、1例は臨床病期B-2で発症していた。全例が当初シスプラチン併用化学療法を受けていた。PC-RPLND前に12例でαフェトプロテイン(AFP)が上昇、3例でβ-hCGが上昇していた。7例は切除時に腫瘍マーカーが上昇していた。7例は切除標本が奇形腫のみで、中央値35か月の時点で全例に病勢の証拠はなかった(NED)。2例は壊死のみで、10か月および42か月時点でNEDであった。6例は切除標本にがんが認められ、2例はNED、1例は病勢を伴って生存、3例は病死した。切除標本にがんを認めた6例のうち5例のみが術後化学療法を受けていた。結論：初回化学療法後に腫瘍マーカーがわずかに上昇した一部の患者では、切除標本が奇形腫または壊死のみのことがある。これらの9例は持続的にNEDである。救援手術で切除標本にがんを認めた患者の予後は不良であるが、適切に選択された患者は本治療法で治癒し、救援化学療法の合併症を回避できる。
